title: Sabzeh: Closing Panel
description: Image credit: Olya Gotlka Sabzeh Closing Panel Sunday, October 19, 11:00 – 1:00 pm Homeroom Gallery 2 | 50 Victoria Street, Aurora All are invited to the galleries for a closing panel and Q&A with several creatives behind the production of Sabzeh, including: Parisa Sabet, Laura Friedmann, Bahia Marks, Rah Eleh, Olya Glotka. A free RSVP is required for all interested in attending. Please complete the form below to reserve your place: 2025 Closing Talk: Sabzeh RSVP Name(Required) First Last Phone(Required)Email(Required) How many people within your group will be attending the workshop?(Required) 1 - Just me! 2 - Me (plus one!) 3 - Me (plus two!) Please provide the following info for each of the additional attendees Name First Last Name First Last Do you or any of your guests require Accessible Seating? Yes No If yes, how many people is the Accessible Seating needed for? Content Notice Please be advised that this live artist talk is an unscripted conversation. While every effort is made to foster respectful dialogue, the views expressed are those of the individual artists and do not necessarily reflect those of the Aurora Cultural Centre. Some discussions may include mature themes or sensitive topics. Featured Artists: Dr. Parisa Sabet is a composer, educator, and artistic leader based in Aurora, Ontario, whose work blends storytelling, social engagement, and sonic innovation. Drawing from her Iranian heritage and Western classical training, she creates music that sparks dialogue and evokes powerful imagery. Her interdisciplinary projects, including Sabzeh and Silent, explore themes of justice, resilience, and cultural identity. A dedicated educator, she founded No Need to Vanish, a platform that makes music technology more accessible to people from beginners to advanced practitioners. Actively engaged in commissions, research, and leadership roles, she remains committed to using music as a bridge across cultures and communities. Laura Friedmann is a Colombian-Canadian multidisciplinary artist whose work bridges fiber art, storytelling, design, and immersive experiences. Her early connection to Colombia’s weaving traditions and background as a filmmaker informs her exploration of legacy, diaspora, human connection, and social change through handcrafted and visual narratives. Laura holds an Honours BFA and a BEd, grounding her work in artistic and educational foundations. She blends traditional craftsmanship with contemporary techniques, drawing from somatic practices in nervous system regulation to emphasize inner alignment, intergenerational healing, resilience, and self-compassion as pathways to collective well-being. Laura lives in Toronto with her husband and two children. Bahia Marks was born and raised in Cape Town, South Africa. Her perspective has been shaped by visiting and living in many places, most recently Brooklyn, New York, and Toronto, Canada. Fascinated by architecture, Bahia contemplates the relationship between built environments and their inhabitants—specifically, how these environments shape our thoughts and actions, both individually and collectively. She states: “the built environment must be designed to facilitate an effective connection with how our physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual faculties function. when people are able to effectively understand and shape their environment, they can build healthy communities and cities that foster a high quality of life.” Bahia is committed to working with communities—urban, rural, formal, and informal—to support agency in shaping their own spaces. She views architecture as a tool for collaboration, problem-solving, and empowerment. Rah Eleh is a visual artist and a PhD candidate at the die Angewandte (University of Applied Arts) in Vienna, Austria. Rah’s work has been exhibited extensively both nationally and internationally at spaces including: Venice Biennale (ECC, Palazzo Mora), The Juno Awards (Canada), National Museum (Oslo, Norway), Vögele Kultur Zentrum, (Pfäffikon, Switzerland), Nuit Blanche (Toronto), Museum London, Vienna Art Week (Austria), Carleton University Art Gallery (Ottawa), Williams College Museum of Art (Williamstown, Massachusetts), Miami Art Basel, Nieuwe Vide (Haarlem, Netherlands), SomoS Art Haus (Berlin, Germany), Kunsthaus Graz Museum (Graz, Austria), and Onassis Cultural Center (Athens, Greece). She has been the recipient of numerous awards including: Long listed for 2023 Sobey Art Award, Chalmers Arts Fellowship, numerous Canada Council, Ontario Arts Council and Toronto Art Council Grants, and SSHRC for her MFA and the CSG Doctoral Fellowship for her PhD. She has been awarded several residencies including the ONX Studio (NYC, NY, 2024), Intergenerational LGBTQ Artist Residency (Toronto Island, 2019), Koumaria Residency (Greece, 2016), MUU Galleria (Helsinki, 2015), Studio Das Weisse Haus (Vienna, 2014) and the Artslant Georgia Fee Residency (Paris). Rah Eleh is represented by de Montigny Contemporary and Vtape, Canada’s leading artist-run distributor for video art. Olya Glotka is a Ukrainian-born, Toronto-based award-winning filmmaker and storyteller. Her in-depth background in theatre, visual arts, creative writing and music gives her well rounded insights in how to tell stories with moving images. Her passion for movement infuses her concept of art. And her growing up in a country in turmoil informs her commitment to use her art form for social and political change. Over the last 7 years Olya directed and shot over 60 short dance films, 5 short form docs, 2 short films and 2 web-series. As well as most recently, a feature documentary film for National Geographic. Deeply passionate about accessibility, diversity, women and 2SLGBTQ+ rights, she has been involved in social work in multiple ways be it through accessibility committees or being a volunteer counselor at a crisis centre.
